shortDescription: By Emily Ou YongJapanese rubber futures fell for a fifth straight session on Tuesday, weighed down by softening tyre demand in China and a technical correction after prices failed to break recent highs, even as oil prices climbed.($1 = 154.7400 yen)($1 = 6.7106 Chinese yuan)

children: Japanese rubber futures fell for a fifth straight session on Tuesday, weighed down by softening tyre demand in China and a technical correction after prices failed to break recent highs, even as oil prices climbed.
The Osaka Exchange (OSE) rubber contract for February delivery
was down 4.2 yen, or 0.98%, at 422.3 yen ($2.73) per kg as of 0155 GMT.
The rubber contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange (SHFE) for January delivery
fell 380 yuan, or 1.99%, to 18,670 yuan ($2,782.17) per metric ton.
The most active October butadiene rubber contract on the SHFE (SHBRv1) plunged 500 yuan, or 3.29%, to 14,675 yuan per metric ton.

Operating rates at downstream tyre makers have weakened as profitability is squeezed, with further declines expected next week as some companies plan holiday closures ahead of National Day and Mid-Autumn Festival, analysts from broker Huatai Futures said in a note.

Natural rubber futures failed to break through previous highs this week and have entered a short-term technical correction, with support from agriculture-linked bullish factors also fading, analysts from broker Gelin Dahua Futures said in a note.
Losses were limited, however, by rising oil prices.

Oil prices rose on Tuesday as concerns over supply disruptions persisted after attacks on Saudi Arabian energy infrastructure left the kingdom's East-West pipeline offline and cast doubt on efforts to ease shipping risks in the Gulf.
Natural rubber often takes direction from oil prices as it competes for market share with synthetic rubber, which is made from crude oil.
The front-month rubber contract on Singapore Exchange's SICOM platform for November delivery (STFX6) last traded at 232.8 U.S. cents per kg, down 1.8%.
